title: Graceful model fallthrough trigger and tenant-isolation circuit policy
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a deterministic yet adaptive mechanism that automatically routes requests to a fallback model variant (fallthrough) when composite operational signals indicate reduced serving quality for a region or tenant. The feature should isolate noisy tenants, provide a probation/soft-open period before reopening, and support sampling probes that validate variant health without large traffic shifts. Goal: reduce end-user error exposure and keep tail latency from cascading across tiers while minimizing unnecessary failovers.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Fallback triggers when composite score > threshold for 30s across a rolling 1m window (signals: 429 rate, error rate, p95 latency, queue depth)
AC2: Tenant isolation policy prevents global failover; high-noise tenant traffic is diverted to a per-tenant fallback with configurable probation windows
AC3: During soft-open, 1% probe traffic validates fallback health; if probes succeed for probation window, system widens traffic in controlled steps
AC4: Circuit enters exponential backoff with decaying threshold on repeated trips; telemetry includes trip reason and normalized score
AC5: Feature gate + toggle exposed in Console with per-project thresholds and observability links
implementation_notes: Composite trigger: compute normalized sub-scores for 429s, error-rate, p95 latency and request backlog; weight = {429:0.4, error:0.3, p95:0.2, backlog:0.1} by default; allow project override
Fallthrough variant selection: prefer lower-cost compatible variant with same tokenizer and similar generation config; maintain model compatibility map in catalog
Probation window: default 60s soft-open with 1% sampling probes; on success, ramp to 10% over 2 minutes then to full traffic if stable
Circuit policy: CLOSED -> OPEN (trip) -> SOFT_OPEN (probes) -> HALF_OPEN trial ramp -> CLOSED; maintain per-tenant and per-region circuits
Decay/rehab: apply exponential decay to trip score over 10m to avoid oscillation; keep minimum cool-down of 30s
Observability: emit event with fields [trip_score, dominant_signal, tenant_id, region, affected_route, fallback_variant, probe_success_rate]

risks: Probe-induced noise: probes themselves could add noise to overloaded clusters; mitigate by strict sampling caps and backpressure-aware scheduling
Oscillation: naive reopen policies can cause flapping; use exponential decay and minimum cool-downs
Incorrect variant selection may change output characteristics for customers; include opt-out and quick rollback via Console
Operational complexity: per-tenant circuits increase state cardinality; design for TTL-driven eviction and aggregated dashboards
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature gated rollout to internal staging with per-route default thresholds and verbose telemetry
Phase 2: Canary on non-critical tenants (10 tenants) for 48h, monitor probe success and revert on >2% user-facing error increase
Phase 3: Gradual expansion by region, enable Console knobs for pilot customers
Phase 4: Full rollout with default thresholds and recommended tuning guide
qa_plan: Automated integration tests for composite score calculation, simulated 429/error/latency spikes to verify trip/open/soft-open transitions; e2e canary with synthetic traffic and human review; add unit tests for decay math and sampling rates.
